correctness.rationale: For every k≥2, h=6k+5, m=5h−1, the proposed finite C_k and periodic B_k+qm satisfy a complete exact greedy partition. The proof reduces distinct three-sums of C_k, mixed 2^C+B, and modular mixed triples to explicit six residue-slice intervals with affine endpoints in k; independent integer set calculations for k=2,3,4,8 reproduced every published C3/P interval and all modular noncollision conditions. On the initial window h<n≤E=11h+3 the admitted values and excluded triple-sums partition every integer; beyond E each excluded value n−m has a triple representation with a periodic summand, so shifting its largest such summand by m preserves distinctness and propagates exclusion. All periodic candidates are protected by modular disjointness; the unique gap 4h−6 per m-block establishes minimal eventual period, and |B_k|=3k+3 gives exact density. Direct independent greedy generation through 12h for k=2,3,4,5,8,13 matched the closed formula. Finite tests alone do not prove the all-k endpoint inequalities, which follow from the affine interval calculations and their k≥2 ordering.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge PASS: van Berkel–Bosma 2026 general t-sumfree eventual-periodicity theorem requires g≥max(f+1,d−1) for triples (f,g,g+d); on this family f=1,g=2,d=h−2, which violates 2≥h−3 for every h≥17. Their isolated computational seed data do not imply a single exact all-k period m=5h−1 and full residue/prefix formula. Shtrezi 2026 proves S_(1,g,g+1), which at g=2 has h=3 and does not intersect h=6k+5≥17. Earlier two-sumfree results use a different excluded sum length. Full van Berkel–Bosma preprint could not be obtained via lawful accessible routes and institutional service reported disconnected VPN; this access limitation is a specific priority risk, not automatic novelty failure.
